title: Parameter Superposition baseline vs structured Mirror contexts
hypothesis: On an aligned synthetic family of task vectors, a learned structured Mirror context code can retrieve multiple tasks from one superposed physical tensor with lower cross-talk than the original fixed random PSP contexts at equal serialized code bytes.
physical_object: one tensor containing a superposition of N task-specific vectors
mirror_coordinate: per-task dense, random PSP, or learned low-dimensional structured context vector; per-dimension unbinding operator
logical_multiplicity: N task vectors reconstructed from one shared stored tensor

task.task_values: independent Gaussian teacher vectors; query evaluation uses held-out Gaussian inputs

controls: Parameter Superposition with fixed seeded Rademacher contexts and coordinatewise unbinding
shared tensor plus task index only
learned 8-dimensional structured context codes trained on development tasks

development.allowed: Development-only check found no eligible hyperparameter: learning rates [0.001, 0.01, 0.1] at 1200 updates all fail the preregistered utility ceiling (relative held-out output NRMSE < 0.25). Do not inspect or run fresh; first revise mechanism under a new MA amendment/ID.

storage.authority: actual torch-serialized inference payload bytes including superposed tensor, context codes, scale, indices, and metadata
paid_objects: all task-specific context vectors or structured codes

success_gate: At N=32, structured Mirror must reduce mean fresh held-out output NRMSE by at least 20% vs fixed PSP at equal-or-lower actual payload bytes in every world; report comparison to explicit task vectors and learned generic codes.
failure_gate: Mirror fails the relative NRMSE/byte gate, or superposition retrieval is not useful (NRMSE >= 0.25).
boundaries: Synthetic aligned Gaussian vector tasks only; this is not a neural-network model composition or NLP capability claim.
Learned Mirror contexts are optimized from development task vectors; fresh task IDs and Gaussian inputs are held out.
Useful multiplicity is based on held-out task output error, not combinatorial code counts.

development_screen.result: Fixed random PSP unbinding NRMSE 1.000; rank-8 learned contexts NRMSE 1.151-1.154 at 19,237B/task; shared tensor without task identity NRMSE 5.805. No model reached utility gate 0.25.
development_screen.decision: Do not access fresh: current task/control protocol is not informative for the planned comparison.

metric_audit_after_development.issue: held-out NRMSE calculation broadcasted [n] and [n,1] tensors into [n,n], invalidating numeric NRMSE values.
metric_audit_after_development.consequence: development metrics are exploratory only; no utility/capacity claim.
